answer: Dynamic opportunity-cost bonds tie each account’s profit to a forfeitable stake, while a subgame-perfect punishment matrix imposes maximal slashing on any Sybil identity multiplication; this forces rational agents’ payoff from spawning duplicates to be strictly negative, eliminating the incentive to wander across forged identities. Consequently, the profile where every participant follows a single thread of identity, like a knoll of trust, is a strict Nash equilibrium that no deviation can profitably exploit.
